security_audit.summary: The review found no evidence of malicious intent, prompt injection, data exfiltration, or hidden execution. Static findings are false positives from Markdown fences, placeholder credentials, documentation links, and quantum optimization terminology. Authors should still clarify credential handling and mark install commands as user-approved steps.

remediation.issue: Placeholder hardware API key appears in a code example.
remediation.suggestion: Replace inline api_key examples with environment-variable guidance and state that real tokens must stay out of shared files.

remediation.issue: Installation snippets include package install commands.
remediation.suggestion: Add a short note that users should review packages and run installation commands only in trusted environments.

remediation.issue: External documentation links can look like network behavior to scanners.
remediation.suggestion: Label them as optional reference links and avoid implying that the skill contacts them automatically.

content.value_statement: Quantum projects need careful circuit, device, and optimizer choices. This skill gives PennyLane patterns for circuits, hybrid models, hardware, and chemistry.
actual_capabilities: Guides PennyLane installation and optional hardware plugin setup with uv pip examples.
Explains QNodes, gates, measurements, templates, and circuit inspection workflows.
Shows hybrid quantum-classical training with optimizers and machine learning framework integration.
Covers VQE, molecular Hamiltonians, UCCSD, and quantum chemistry workflows.
Compares simulator and hardware backend setup for IBM, Braket, Cirq, Rigetti, and IonQ.
Summarizes gradient methods, optimizer choices, barren plateaus, and QAOA patterns.
limitations: It is documentation guidance, not a managed PennyLane runtime.
Hardware execution requires provider accounts, credentials, quotas, and available devices.
Examples may need updates for your PennyLane version and selected plugin.
It does not prove quantum advantage or guarantee production performance.

use_cases.title: Prototype quantum circuits
use_cases.description: Create QNodes, select simulators, inspect measurements, and move stable circuits toward hardware backends.

use_cases.title: Design hybrid learning experiments
use_cases.description: Plan data encoding, variational layers, training loops, and framework integration for quantum machine learning studies.

use_cases.title: Prepare chemistry simulations
use_cases.description: Outline VQE, molecular Hamiltonian, ansatz, and optimizer choices before running molecular energy experiments.

prompt_templates.title: Start a PennyLane project
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me set up a PennyLane workflow for a two-qubit circuit. Include installation steps, a simple QNode, and result inspection.

prompt_templates.title: Build a variational classifier
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a PennyLane variational classifier for a small labeled dataset. Recommend data encoding, ansatz shape, optimizer, and validation checks.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a chemistry VQE run
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a PennyLane VQE experiment for a simple molecule. Explain the Hamiltonian, ansatz, optimizer, convergence checks, and common failure modes.

prompt_templates.title: Compare hardware backends
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare simulator and hardware backend choices for a four-qubit PennyLane workflow. Include credentials, shots, gradients, costs, and fallback testing steps.

output_examples.input: I need to choose a PennyLane device for a four-qubit prototype.
output: A simulator-first recommendation using default.qubit or lightning.qubit for early validation.
A hardware readiness checklist covering provider credentials, shot counts, supported operations, queue behavior, and cost controls.
A migration plan that keeps the circuit interface stable while swapping backend devices.

output_examples.input: I want to train a quantum classifier with PennyLane.
output: A workflow covering feature scaling, data encoding, ansatz depth, optimizer choice, and metric tracking.
A risk note about barren plateaus, overfitting, and interface mismatches between array libraries.
Validation steps for gradient checks, baseline comparisons, and repeatable runs.

output_examples.input: I need a VQE plan for a small molecule.
output: A chemistry workflow that identifies geometry, electron count, active space, ansatz, and Hamiltonian setup.
An optimization plan with convergence criteria, restart strategy, and simulator validation before hardware use.
A result review checklist for energy units, reference values, and sensitivity to ansatz choices.

best_practices: Start every workflow on a simulator, then move only validated circuits to paid or queued hardware.
Store provider credentials outside notebooks, prompts, and shared examples.
Track interfaces, seeds, shots, gradients, and optimizer settings for repeatable experiments.
anti_patterns: Submitting hardware jobs before checking circuit behavior on local simulators.
Hard-coding API tokens or provider keys in examples, notebooks, or prompts.
Changing optimizer, backend, and ansatz at the same time without a baseline.

faq.question: Can this skill execute quantum circuits?
faq.answer: No. It provides PennyLane guidance and examples. Execution requires a local Python environment with PennyLane installed.

faq.question: Does it support Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows.

faq.question: Can it help with hardware backends?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers simulator and hardware concepts for IBM, Amazon Braket, Google Cirq, Rigetti, IonQ, and related plugins.

faq.question: Will it handle provider credentials?
faq.answer: No. Keep credentials in secure local storage or environment variables. Do not paste tokens into shared prompts.

faq.question: Is it useful for quantum chemistry?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes VQE, molecular Hamiltonians, UCCSD, and chemistry workflow guidance.

faq.question: Does it guarantee quantum advantage?
faq.answer: No. It helps structure experiments, but performance depends on the problem, device noise, ansatz, and optimizer.
